title: Launch of Nymo x Homey: for dynamic pricing and integration of WaterAccu, home battery, and EV charger
excerpt: The launch of the Nymo x Homey integration means that the WaterAccu can now also be controlled based on dynamic pricing.
contentHtml:
Energy management is becoming increasingly complex: solar panels, home batteries, EV chargers, and dynamic pricing. This has resulted in a proliferation of control apps, while everything needs to be coordinated. Add to that the fact that the net metering scheme is being phased out, and the urgency is clear: solar panel owners are looking for an affordable and future-proof plan. Homey and Solyx Energy are joining forces for the next step in smart energy management.

The missing link for solar panel owners

Thanks to the collaboration between two Dutch innovators, Homey and Solyx Energy, households can now also control their water battery via a single central app. Using simple rules, or flows, as Homey calls them, you can go as crazy as you want. Give priority to the EV charger on Monday, save gas on Tuesday using solar panels, and take advantage of negative dynamic prices on Wednesday. That is now possible.

The golden triangle after 2027

2.7 million Dutch households have solar panels, supplying an average of 70% of the energy they generate. With the net metering scheme set to be abolished in 2027, solutions are needed. Timing the dishwasher is a no-brainer, but has limited impact. In fact, there are three major steps that solar panel owners can take: the home battery, an electric car, and the water battery. The interesting thing about these three steps is that, in the long term, they can function alongside each other. Households can therefore expand over time and spread their investments.

The home battery is the best-known solution, but it is expensive. Plug-in batteries are gaining popularity, but their storage capacity is limited. Electric cars are ideal as batteries on wheels for utilizing surplus solar energy. However, even if you have an electric car, it is not always plugged in at midday. The third option, the water battery (or solar power boiler), is much less well known. Yet this is the least expensive solution, which also saves gas.

The water battery and the revival of the electric boiler

The water storage tank, also known as a solar power boiler, consists of the Nymo from Solyx Energy and a regular electric boiler. A boiler for a three-person household stores around 10kWh, so it has much more storage capacity than most home batteries. The Nymo is a smart dimmer that ensures that the boiler is only heated using unused solar energy, i.e., electricity that would otherwise be fed back into the grid. The water battery is particularly suitable for households that currently heat their water with gas, using a central heating combi boiler. The result: showering with solar energy instead of gas. The cost: around €1,250, while the annual savings can easily amount to €300-400 per year.

Electric boilers lost ground for years because heat pumps are more efficient. But in a world with increasing amounts of solar power, boilers are becoming popular again. No gas, no waste of solar energy, and a perfect buffer that helps absorb peaks and troughs in the electricity grid. The water storage tank is therefore not a battery for storing electricity, but stores hot water that households use for showering.

Dynamic pricing and integration with other devices

“Since our launch last year, more than 750 Nymo WaterAccu units have been installed. Customers are delighted with the simplicity and ease of use—you don’t have to worry about a thing,” says Emma Snaak, co-founder of Solyx Energy. “Thanks to our collaboration with Homey, we now also offer the two most requested features: dynamic price control and full integration with other systems in the home.”

Controlling the water battery based on dynamic energy prices is interesting because it allows the system to be used to its full potential in winter, when there is little surplus solar energy. In addition, the collaboration makes the water battery future-proof: Homey has the widest range of integrations, so if you invest in a home battery or EV charger in the future, everything can be controlled via the same app.
